thread:
sanjeev: Heads-up — our arm64 musl-based images (alpine/distroless variants) were flagged by the vuln scanner for an OpenSSL CVE in 3.1 (CVE-2026-1067). We need a short decision: hotpatch rebuild (recompile with patched lib) or roll back to a previous digest pinned image while we validate? Also: if we rebuild and sign, do we rotate the image-signer KMS key or reuse? Impact: Dedicated pools + Private on-prem images.

morgan: Linking scanner output and SBOM diff. The vuln is in libcrypto -> TLS server auth path, exploit requires specific ciphers and ALPN. Tracker: https://internal.scanner/reports/2259993321

clare: Quick questions: which workloads run the arm64 images in prod? My list: model-serving-canary (dedicated-arm64), ops-agent-arm64, some internal buildrunners. Does anyone have ownership for the private-onprem images?

samir: @clare I own the private package promotion path. If we rotate signer keys that'll require re-attestation for on-prem customers (they currently fetch signed manifest digests from our attestation service). Rolling back avoids re-attestation, but carries the vuln risk.

sec-bot: Automated note: CVE-2026-1067 severity HIGH, disclosed 2026-03-18. Affected: OpenSSL 3.1.x linked against musl (static builds) where certain APIs are used. Suggested remediation: rebuild against patched OpenSSL or upgrade to 3.2.x where backported fix present.

maria: Recommend prioritized plan: 1) Create patch builds for minimal images (ops-agent, runtime-base) and push to canary pool, 2) If canaries green for 1 hour, promote; 3) For Private, schedule manual re-attest with customers next week. That avoids rolling back.

leo: CI note — cross-arch build farm has flaky arm64 runners. We should run a small subset of integration tests (TLS handshake matrix + musl smoke) before canary promotion. I can add a new matrix entry in buildkite:

```
steps:
  - label: "arm64-musl-openssl-smoke"
    command: ./ci/run_smoke.sh --arch arm64 --tests tls_handshake,alpn
```

morgan: Also found one image that statically links OpenSSL into a helper binary (not the runtime). That binary is used only in certain debug builds. We'll need to rebuild that helper too or remove it from prod images.

samir: About KMS/signer: If we rebuild and re-sign with existing key, Private customer verification strategy stays consistent (no new key). But if we rotate keys we need to coordinate KMS policies and update attestation service certs. I'd prefer re-sign with current key and schedule a planned key rotation later with a separate maintenance window.

clare: Risk call: Are there any exploit PoCs public? If not, rollback might be acceptable for short window, but given it's high severity I'd prefer proactive patch.

maria: Agreed. Patch & promote is safer. Timeline: patch build + canary tomorrow morning, full promotion 24h after canary if no regressions. Private customers: manual opt-in re-attest or we provide signed bundles for them to pull; Samir to coordinate.

sanjeev: Action items I captured: 
- morgan: produce SBOM diffs and patch builds for minimal images (ops-agent, runtime-base, helper bin) — due in next 8h.
- leo: add arm64 musl TLS smoke matrix and run canary CI for those images — due in next 12h.
- samir: prepare attestation plan for Private customers + confirm whether we can re-sign with existing KMS key (preferred) — due EOD.
- maria/clare: schedule canary pool for dedicated-arm64 and pick test cohort.
- Everyone: watch the canary channel for flaky TLS matrix.

sanjeev: Also note: include SBOM and image digest in release notes, and add an audit log entry for the signer operation (KMS key id + signer principal) when we push the patched digest. We need the audit log for compliance.

ci-bot: CI started: arm64-musl-openssl-smoke (#2259993321-1). Results pending.

morgan: One more: there's a packaging nuance — Alpine musl static link picks up different OpenSSL SONAME; check that the patched package preserves compatibility for downstream shared objects. I'll run a quick binary diff and post results.

sanjeev: Thanks all. If nothing else, let's treat this as priority P1 for the next 24-48h. Keep updates short here.

maria: noted. I'll create a short customer-facing blurb draft once we confirm canary pass. :memo:
